question.text: A novel type of PET radiotracer is being developed to evaluate patients with Parkinson’s disease. A clinical research study has enrolled 1,200 patients, half of whom have the disease. The scan is found to be positive in 590 of the 600 patients with known PD, and positive in 20 of the 600 patients without PD. What is the test’s overall specificity?

In this case, 580 patients without PD had negative scans (600 total without PD - 20 positive = 580 negative). The denominator should be all individuals without PD (600), so specificity = 580/600 = 580/(580+20).

Here, true negatives are the 20 patients without PD who were correctly identified as negative (scan negative), and false positives are the 20 patients without PD who were incorrectly identified as positive (scan positive). The 590 positives among PD patients are assumed to be true positives (since all PD patients should be positive for a perfect test). Thus, specificity = 20 / (20 + 590).
